content.text:
All 12 pass, including the oracle-uniformity and replay tests.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- The nonce is committed **before** the email token and is deliberately *not* rolled back when the token check fails. That ordering is what makes the proof single-use in its own right rather than "single-use if the other factor happened to hold" — a captured envelope replayed later against a token the attacker has since obtained lands on a nonce already seen.
- The existence gate (`account_password_hash`'s outer `None`) runs before signature verification on both branches. That's not just tidiness: without it, an unauthenticated caller could make Custos fetch an arbitrary DID's plc.directory audit log — turning the endpoint into a request-amplification lever. `sovereign_session.rs` guards the same way.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

input.title: Hoist decode_canonical_base64url to a shared auth helper
input.tldr: Three route files now each carry an identical copy of the canonical-base64url decoder that guards signed-proof nonces and signatures. Moving it into one place stops the copies drifting.
input.prompt:
`decode_canonical_base64url` (and the `SIGNATURE_BYTES`/`NONCE_BYTES` constants beside it) is now duplicated verbatim in three PDS route files:

- crates/pds/src/routes/sovereign_session.rs
- crates/pds/src/routes/oauth_consent.rs
- crates/pds/src/routes/delete_account.rs

It is a security primitive — it enforces that a nonce/signature is exactly N bytes in *canonical* unpadded base64url (re-encoding must reproduce the input), so a proof cannot be re-spelled into a fresh nonce. Three copies is three places for that check to drift.

Per crates/pds/AGENTS.md, routes must not import from other routes; shared pure logic belongs in `auth/` (Functional Core). Hoist the function and the two constants into a small module there (e.g. `crates/pds/src/auth/signed_proof.rs`, `// pattern: Functional Core`), have all three routes use it, and move the unit coverage with it. Keep the behaviour byte-identical — every one of these routes' existing tests must still pass unchanged (`cargo test -p pds sovereign_session oauth_consent delete_account`).

content.content:
### `optionalPassword`

An account can be created on this server with no password at all. A client that
sees this capability may omit the password field entirely when creating an
account; the account is stored with no password hash and authenticates
afterwards through its device key — wallet-confirmed OAuth consent and sovereign
sessions — plus app passwords for standard AT Protocol clients like the Bluesky
app.

Passwordless accounts are not a new storage shape: accounts that migrate in from
another server have always been stored without a password. What this capability
changes is only whether a *new* account may be created that way.

An **empty** password is refused whether or not this is enabled, and that is
deliberate: an empty string is what an uninitialised form field sends, so
accepting one would let a client bug create an account with no credential that
nobody asked for. Omitting the field is the only way to ask.

**Controlled by:** `accounts.password_optional`. Off by default — a passwordless
account depends on device-key custody you cannot verify on the account holder's
behalf, so a deployment whose users are not all running the identity wallet
should keep the password required. Enable it with `[accounts] password_optional =
true` (`EZPDS_ACCOUNTS_PASSWORD_OPTIONAL`) and the capability appears. Turning it
back off stops new passwordless accounts being created; it does not affect
accounts that already have no password, which keep working exactly as before.

### `didWebHosting`

Custos serves an opted-in account's `did:web` document at the account's own
domain (`/.well-known/did.json`) and emits an identity event so relays re-resolve
after an edit.

Hosting is opt-in **per account**, never automatic, and only ever for a domain
the user controls: moving the document onto Custos trades away some of the
independence a self-hosted document gives an identity, so it is the account
holder's decision. Exit is a DNS repoint away.

**Controlled by:** always. The server-side capability is inherent to running
Custos and has no operator switch; whether any given account uses it is that
account holder's choice.

### `waitlist`

A public interest-signup waitlist for a pre-launch deployment: an unauthenticated
`POST /waitlist` accepting an email address plus an optional atproto handle, meant
to be posted to directly from a marketing page on another origin (the endpoint is
CORS-open and carries no credentials). Signups are idempotent per email — a repeat
returns the same success and never discloses whether an address was already on the
list — and the handle is syntax-checked but deliberately never resolved, so the
endpoint has no outbound-request surface. The operator reads the list back with
`GET /v1/admin/waitlist` (newest first, with a total), which keeps working even
after the public endpoint is switched off again.

**Controlled by:** `waitlist.enabled`. Off by default — an instance that isn't
running a launch funnel should not carry a public write endpoint it never asked
for. Enable it with `[waitlist] enabled = true` (`EZPDS_WAITLIST_ENABLED`) and the
capability appears; the per-IP signup rate cap is `rate_limit.waitlist_per_5min`
(`EZPDS_RATE_LIMIT_WAITLIST_PER_5MIN`, default 30).

input.new_string:
### `walletAccountDelete`

An account can be permanently deleted with a device-key-signed proof from one of
its current rotation keys, in place of the account password. The emailed
single-use confirmation code is still required — this swaps one of the two
factors, it does not remove one.

This capability is what makes `optionalPassword` safe to turn on. Deletion is the
one operation that had no route around the password: an account created without
one could be made, used, and migrated, but never removed, because every
credential path answered with the same refusal and left the holder no way
forward. The proof closes that.

The signed envelope binds this server, the account, the signing key, the moment,
and a single-use nonce, and it is verified against the identity's **authoritative**
current rotation set read live from plc.directory — never a cached document. It is
accepted for accounts that *do* have a password too: a current rotation key can
already migrate or retire the identity outright, so it is the stronger credential,
and honouring only the weaker one would make the endpoint answer differently
depending on whether a password exists. Unknown accounts, wrong passwords, and bad
proofs remain one indistinguishable response.

**Controlled by:** always. This is the same key-sovereign trust model as
`sovereignSessions` and has no operator switch; password-based deletion continues
to work unchanged for accounts that have a password.

I'm defining a credential enum for the wallet's account deletion endpoint, which will support both password-based deletion and device-key-signed proofs for accounts that advertise the wallet account delete capability.

I'll keep the HTTPS guard unconditional since both the deletion token and proof need protection in transit, then update the reasoning in the documentation. For signing the envelope, I need the server DID from describing the server, the account DID, a device key ID from the identity store, and a signer closure, along with a fresh timestamp and nonce. The frontend should prevent this based on the same capability check, but it's good defensive programming to have the error anyway. content.thinking:
I'm noticing that the `pds_capabilities::probe` function caches results per host, which could cause issues in tests where different mock servers run on different ports. The test `a_host_without_the_capability_refuses_a_passwordless_removal` caches an empty capabilities response, but I need to verify the correct httpmock API for checking call counts — it looks like the existing test uses `assert_calls(0)` rather than `.calls()`.

I should also consider whether the probe gets called again if the cache is warm from a previous test at the same base URL, though different ports should prevent that collision. I'll switch to using `assert_calls(1)` to be explicit. The `build_delete_credential` function probes capabilities before touching the keychain, so I don't strictly need to call `add_identity` in the test, but I'll leave it for consistency. I also need to verify that `PdsClient::new_for_test` is available and whether the wallet host tests will compile without SDKROOT set up.

Looking at the network calls more carefully: if I call `probe` first, it makes one request and caches the result, then calling `describe_server` explicitly makes another request. That's two network calls when I could optimize to one by calling `describe_server` first to warm the cache and get the server DID, then extracting capabilities directly from the response's `custos` field. This avoids the redundant cache dependency and keeps things cleaner.

For the test, I'll assert that `describe_server` is called exactly once. But I need to reconsider the error handling — if the host is unreachable, we should surface that as a network error rather than a password requirement, which is more honest about what actually happened.

<script lang="ts">
  import { onMount } from 'svelte';
  import {
    requestIdentityRemoval,
    confirmIdentityRemoval,
    tombstoneIdentity,
    listPendingRemovals,
    forgetIdentityLocally,
    isCodedError,
    type RemovalError,
    type RemovalOutcome,
  } from '$lib/ipc';
  import { unlockIdentity, isUnlockCancelled } from '$lib/unlock';
  import { authenticateBiometric } from '$lib/biometric';
  import { truncateDid } from '$lib/did-doc-utils';
  import { didWebDocumentUrl } from '$lib/did-web';
  import Button from '$lib/components/ui/Button.svelte';
  import TextField from '$lib/components/ui/TextField.svelte';
  import Spinner from '$lib/components/ui/Spinner.svelte';
  import ChevronLeftIcon from '$lib/components/ui/ChevronLeftIcon.svelte';
  import { useHoldGesture } from '$lib/components/ui/use-hold-gesture.svelte';

  let {
    did,
    handle,
    onback,
    oncomplete,
  }: {
    did: string;
    /** The identity's handle (for context in the warning); may be empty. */
    handle?: string;
    onback: () => void;
    /** Called on success. `wasLast` routes back to onboarding vs. the identity list. */
    oncomplete: (wasLast: boolean) => void;
  } = $props();

  // warn → confirm (code + password) → (on partial failure) tombstone_retry.
  // forget_confirm is the local-only escape hatch, reachable whenever the server-side
  // deletion can't proceed (the account no longer exists on its PDS).
  // web_epilogue is the did:web terminal state: the removal succeeded, but the last step
  // — taking the DID's document off the domain — belongs to the user, not the wallet.
  type Phase =
    | 'warn'
    | 'requesting'
    | 'confirm'
    | 'working'
    | 'tombstone_retry'
    | 'forget_confirm'
    | 'web_epilogue';
  let phase = $state<Phase>('warn');
  let error = $state<string | null>(null);

  // A did:web has no PLC tombstone: it is retired by removing its document from the
  // domain, which the wallet has no control over. That single fact drives every copy
  // branch on this screen — what the warning promises, whether the "also retire on the
  // network" advanced option exists at all, and how a removal ends.
  let isDidWeb = $derived(did.startsWith('did:web:'));
  // The document's authoritative URL, for a concrete instruction rather than a vague one.
  // `didWebDocumentUrl` throws on a malformed identifier — fall back to naming no URL
  // rather than blocking the epilogue over cosmetics.
  let didWebDocUrl = $derived.by(() => {
    if (!isDidWeb) return null;
    try {
      return didWebDocumentUrl(did);
    } catch {
      return null;
    }
  });

  // Carried from the successful removal into `web_epilogue`, so the Done button routes
  // exactly where an immediate `oncomplete` would have.
  let epilogueWasLast = $state(false);

  let code = $state('');
  let password = $state('');

  let canConfirm = $derived(code.trim().length > 0 && password.length > 0);

  // If a prior attempt already deleted the PDS account but was interrupted before the
  // tombstone + wipe finished (the app was killed mid-flow), the account is gone and the
  // single-use email code is spent — the request flow would fail. Resume straight to the
  // tombstone-only retry instead. Checked on every mount so this self-corrects no matter
  // how the screen was reached (launch reconciliation or manual navigation).
  onMount(async () => {

These diagnostics are just artifacts from the worktree setup—I'll run a proper validation with `pnpm check` once I install node_modules through the main devenv. For the Svelte screen, I'm updating the logic to load the removal route on mount and set `requiresPassword`, then making `canConfirm` depend on whether the code is filled in and the password is provided if needed, while hiding the password field when it's not required.

I'm also updating the confirmation call to pass the password conditionally, adding the new codes to the message handler, and adjusting the warning copy. The tricky part is handling the brief window before the route loads—I'll default `removalRoute` to null and treat that as unknown, so the warning copy branches on whether `requiresPassword` is actually known, avoiding the flash of "and your password" before the network call completes. Since the confirm phase is only reached after `requestIdentityRemoval` returns, the route should be loaded by then anyway.

For the warning copy itself, I'm splitting it into two parts: the email confirmation sentence always shows, then conditionally add either the password clause or the neutral version depending on whether the route has loaded and what `requiresPassword` says. This way there's no misleading flash—before the load, users just see the first sentence.

# Changelog fragments

Every pull request that changes a shipped surface must add a short Markdown fragment:

```text
changelog.d/<id>.<type>.md
```

- `<id>` is the Linear issue identifier in lowercase (for example, `mm-358`). If a
  change has no Linear issue, use the pull request number (for example, `271`).
- `<type>` is one of `added`, `changed`, `fixed`, `removed`, or `security`.
- The file contains one concise, user- or operator-facing Markdown statement. Do not
  include a heading or bullet marker; the release script supplies both.
- Use more than one fragment when a change belongs in more than one category.

Example (`changelog.d/mm-358.added.md`):

```markdown
Release notes now collect user-visible changes from pull requests automatically.
```
=== gate ===
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Require a changelog fragment *added by the change itself* when a PR changes a shipped
# surface (fragments already sitting in changelog.d/ from other work don't satisfy it).
# CHANGELOG_BASE_REF is set to the PR base SHA in CI; an explicit first argument is
# convenient for local checks. With neither, fragment validity is still checked but
# presence is not required because there is no trustworthy comparison range.
set -euo pipefail

cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."

base_ref="${1:-${CHANGELOG_BASE_REF:-}}"
fragment_dir="changelog.d"
fragment_re='^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*\.(added|changed|fixed|removed|security)\.md$'

fail=0
fragment_count=0
while IFS= read -r fragment; do
  name="${fragment##*/}"
  if ! [[ "$name" =~ $fragment_re ]]; then
    echo "✗ invalid changelog fragment '$fragment' — expected <id>.<added|changed|fixed|removed|security>.md" >&2
    fail=1
    continue
  fi
  if ! grep -q '[^[:space:]]' "$fragment"; then
    echo "✗ changelog fragment '$fragment' is empty" >&2
    fail=1
    continue
  fi
  fragment_count=$((fragment_count + 1))
done < <(find "$fragment_dir" -maxdepth 1 -type f -name '*.md' ! -name README.md | sort)

if [ "$fail" -ne 0 ]; then
  exit 1
fi

if [ -z "$base_ref" ]; then
  echo "✓ $fragment_count valid changelog fragment(s); no base ref supplied, so presence was not evaluated"
  exit 0
fi

input.new_string:
body:json {
  {
    "did": "{{did}}",
    "password": "your-account-password",
    "token": "token-from-requestAccountDelete"
  }
}

vars:pre-request {
  baseUrl: http://localhost:8080
}

docs {
  Permanently deletes the account named by `did` after verifying a credential factor and a
  single-use email `token` (obtained from `requestAccountDelete`). This endpoint is NOT
  session-authenticated: the credentials are in the body, so a user can delete an account they can
  no longer log a session into.

  The credential factor is whichever the request presents:

  1. **`password`** — the standard lexicon field, as in the body above.

  2. **A Custos deletion proof** — the off-lexicon `custos.proof` object, for an account created
     with no password at all (the `optionalPassword` capability). Advertised as the
     `walletAccountDelete` capability in `describeServer`. Send `password` as the empty string —
     the vendored lexicon marks the field required, so it stays on the wire — and add:

     ```json
     {
       "did": "{{did}}",
       "password": "",
       "token": "token-from-requestAccountDelete",
       "custos": {
         "proof": {
           "signingKey": "did:key:zDnae...",
           "timestamp": 1753600000,
           "nonce": "<32 random bytes, canonical unpadded base64url>",
           "signature": "<64-byte r||s, canonical unpadded base64url>"
         }
       }
     }
     ```

     `signature` covers `crypto::encode_account_delete_envelope(serverDid, did, signingKey,
     timestamp, nonce)` — the domain-versioned, length-prefixed envelope shared with the wallet
     (golden vector: `test-vectors/account-delete-envelope-v1.json`). `signingKey` must be in the
     account's **authoritative current** signing authority — a did:plc's live plc.directory
     rotation set, or a self-hosted did:web's `#device` key — never merely in the cached DID
     document. The timestamp must be within the freshness window, and each nonce is accepted once
     per DID. A proof is accepted for a passworded account too.

  On success every local trace of the account is removed — repo blocks/blobs (including on-disk
  blob files), sessions, tokens, handles, DID-doc cache, preferences, app passwords, and the
  account row — and an `#account` firehose frame (active=false, status="deleted") is broadcast so
  relays drop the repo. The did:plc identity itself is left intact on plc.directory (the wallet
  owns the rotation key and can tombstone or migrate it independently), matching ezpds's
  wallet-native model.

  Every credential failure — unknown DID, no password on file, wrong password, malformed or stale
  proof, bad signature, unauthorized signing key, replayed nonce — returns one uniform 401, so the
  endpoint is not an account-existence or credential-shape oracle. An invalid/expired token returns
  401; a request carrying neither a password nor a proof returns 400. No credential failure
  consumes the email token. The 200 no-op applies only when the account passes both checks but is
  purged (by the scheduled-deletion reaper or a racing duplicate request) before this handler's own
  delete runs — an account that is already fully gone before the credential check instead returns
  401.
}

  single-use email `token` (obtained from `requestAccountDelete`). This endpoint is NOT
  session-authenticated: the credentials are in the body, so a user can delete an account they can
  no longer log a session into.

  The credential factor is whichever the request presents:

  1. **`password`** — the standard lexicon field, as in the body above.

  2. **A Custos deletion proof** — the off-lexicon `custos.proof` object, for an account created
     with no password at all (the `optionalPassword` capability). Advertised as the
     `walletAccountDelete` capability in `describeServer`. Send `password` as the empty string —
     the vendored lexicon marks the field required, so it stays on the wire — and add:

     ```json
     {
       "did": "{{did}}",
       "password": "",
       "token": "token-from-requestAccountDelete",
       "custos": {
         "proof": {
           "signingKey": "did:key:zDnae...",
           "timestamp": 1753600000,
           "nonce": "<32 random bytes, canonical unpadded base64url>",
           "signature": "<64-byte r||s, canonical unpadded base64url>"
         }
       }
     }
     ```

     `signature` covers `crypto::encode_account_delete_envelope(serverDid, did, signingKey,
     timestamp, nonce)` — the domain-versioned, length-prefixed envelope shared with the wallet
     (golden vector: `test-vectors/account-delete-envelope-v1.json`). `signingKey` must be in the
     account's **authoritative current** signing authority — a did:plc's live plc.directory
     rotation set, or a self-hosted did:web's `#device` key — never merely in the cached DID
     document. The timestamp must be within the freshness window, and each nonce is accepted once
     per DID. A proof is accepted for a passworded account too.

  On success every local trace of the account is removed — repo blocks/blobs (including on-disk
  blob files), sessions, tokens, handles, DID-doc cache, preferences, app passwords, and the
  account row — and an `#account` firehose frame (active=false, status="deleted") is broadcast so
  relays drop the repo. The did:plc identity itself is left intact on plc.directory (the wallet
  owns the rotation key and can tombstone or migrate it independently), matching ezpds's
  wallet-native model.

  Every credential failure — unknown DID, no password on file, wrong password, malformed or stale
  proof, bad signature, unauthorized signing key, replayed nonce — returns one uniform 401, so the
  endpoint is not an account-existence or credential-shape oracle. An invalid/expired token returns
  401; a request carrying neither a password nor a proof returns 400. No credential failure
  consumes the email token. The 200 no-op applies only when the account passes both checks but is
  purged (by the scheduled-deletion reaper or a racing duplicate request) before this handler's own
  delete runs — an account that is already fully gone before the credential check instead returns
  401.
}

lines: - **V045**: Normalizes existing `accounts.email` / `pending_accounts.email` rows to lowercase (trimmed) in place — a data-only migration, no schema change. Both columns already carry a UNIQUE index (`idx_accounts_email` / `idx_pending_accounts_email`), so the normalizing `UPDATE` fails loudly (aborting the whole migration transaction) if two rows would collide once normalized, rather than silently merging them; an operator must resolve the collision manually before the migration can apply. Pairs with the normalize-on-every-read/write-path fix in `uniqueness.rs` (`normalize_email`, shared by `email_taken`) and `accounts.rs` (`resolve_by_email`, `update_account_email`) — the reference PDS lowercases emails on store and lookup, and without this the account-creation routes' byte-exact matching let a differently-cased signup email silently fail later matches (e.g. `requestPasswordReset` 200-and-no-op with no way to discover the mismatch).

- **V044**: Adds nullable `did_web_hosting_enabled_at` TEXT to `accounts` — the opt-in flag for Custos-managed did:web hosting. Derived-status doctrine (V008/V026/V004): NULL = hosting off (never enabled or turned back off); a timestamp = when it was last enabled. The `.well-known/did.json` serve route (`routes/did_json.rs`) reads through this column joined to `did_documents` and the active-lifecycle gate (`dids::serve_hosted_did_document`), so an account that isn't opted in 404s exactly like an unknown host — no opt-in existence oracle. did:plc accounts never set it (their document lives on plc.directory). Writers/readers in `dids.rs`: `set_did_web_hosting` (toggle), `did_web_hosting_enabled` (probe), `serve_hosted_did_document` (gated serve). The opt-in toggle + the authenticated non-PLC document-edit path (direct `did_documents` overwrite via `rewrite_did_document` + `#identity` firehose frame) live in `routes/did_web_hosting.rs`.

-- **V043**: Adds `sovereign_session_nonces`, a dedicated DID-scoped anti-replay store for sovereign-session signed requests. Its `(did, nonce)` primary key makes insert-if-absent atomic and permits the same random nonce across different identities; the DID FK binds rows to hosted accounts, and `idx_sovereign_session_nonces_seen_at` supports bounded stale-row cleanup. The query layer rejects a retention threshold at or below the full `2 * SOVEREIGN_TIMESTAMP_WINDOW_SECS` replay-acceptance span, so sweeping cannot reopen a replay while its signed timestamp is still acceptable. It deliberately does not reuse `admin_nonces`, whose rows are owned by admin device ids.

+- **V043**: Adds `sovereign_session_nonces`, a dedicated DID-scoped anti-replay store for sovereign-session signed requests. Its `(did, nonce)` primary key makes insert-if-absent atomic and permits the same random nonce across different identities; the DID FK binds rows to hosted accounts, and `idx_sovereign_session_nonces_seen_at` supports bounded stale-row cleanup. The query layer rejects a retention threshold at or below the full `2 * SOVEREIGN_TIMESTAMP_WINDOW_SECS` replay-acceptance span, so sweeping cannot reopen a replay while its signed timestamp is still acceptable. It deliberately does not reuse `admin_nonces`, whose rows are owned by admin device ids. It **is** shared by every wallet-signed account proof, not only sovereign sessions: `deleteAccount`'s deletion proof spends its nonce here too. The domain-versioned envelopes make a nonce non-transferable between surfaces anyway, so sharing only strengthens the property (one nonce, one proof, per DID) and keeps these rows on the account-purge path already covered by the schema-walking test rather than adding a table to remember.

- **V042**: Seeds the identity wallet's **canonical** OAuth client row: client_id `https://identitywallet.obsign.org/oauth/client-metadata.json` with redirect URI `org.obsign.identitywallet:/oauth/callback` — the reverse-FQDN scheme⇄host pairing the atproto OAuth spec requires for a native client's private-use redirect (and third-party AS's like bsky.social enforce; the PAR handler now enforces it too for discoverable clients). The wallet's OAuth identity is this fixed URL (it no longer varies with the configured Custos); seeding the row lets any instance accept the wallet without an outbound fetch of the canonical document. Uses `ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE` (corrects a previously cached copy). The V013 row is deliberately kept so pre-transition wallet builds (old client_id + old scheme) keep working. The client-metadata route (`routes/oauth_client_metadata.rs`) serves the same canonical document, with a loopback-`public_url` exception for local dev.

- **Operator transfer visibility/cancel** (no new migration — extends V027/V029/V030 semantics): `transfers.status` gains a new **terminal** value, `cancelled` (operator interruption). No schema change is needed: the column is unconstrained TEXT, and both partial UNIQUE indexes (`idx_transfers_active_did`/`idx_transfers_active_code`) enumerate the *active* statuses, so a cancelled row frees the per-DID and per-code slots exactly like `complete`/`expired`, and every accept/complete lookup (which filters on the active list) ignores it. `transfers.rs` gains `list_inflight_transfers` (the operator view: `accepted`/`completing` rows regardless of expiry — completion has no expiry predicate, so a lapsed accepted transfer can still finish — plus unexpired `pending`; `(created_at, id)` keyset pages; deliberately never selects `code`, a live account-takeover credential), `mark_transfer_cancelled` (UPDATE guarded on the active statuses), and `revoke_transfer_device` (single-credential `revoked_at` tombstone, V030 doctrine). The cross-table cancel transaction (sweep-if-lapsed → cancel → tombstone accepted credential → `transfer.cancelled` audit event) lives in the root `transfer.rs::cancel_transfer`, backing `GET /v1/admin/transfers` + `POST /v1/admin/transfers/{id}/cancel` (`routes/admin_transfers.rs`).

- **V041**: Adds nullable `revoked_at` TEXT to `claim_codes` plus a composite `(created_at, code)` index — operator revocation for a minted-but-unredeemed claim code (a live signup credential). Derived-status doctrine (V004/V025): NULL = never revoked; every redemption path (the atomic single-use UPDATEs in `register_device.rs`/`create_account_xrpc.rs`/`create_mobile_account.rs` and the `claim_code_valid` preflight) additionally requires `revoked_at IS NULL`, so revocation closes redemption exactly like expiry, and the row survives as the audit record. Deliberately an in-place ALTER, not a rebuild: `pending_accounts.claim_code` (V005) FK-references `claim_codes (code)`, so a DROP/rename rebuild fails on any DB holding pending rows; the inventory therefore pages on the immutable `(created_at, code)` keyset (stable across VACUUM — this TEXT-keyed table's implicit rowid is not). `claim_codes.rs` gains `list_claim_codes` (newest-first keyset page, `is_expired` evaluated in SQL so "now" is derived once) and `revoke_claim_code` (guarded UPDATE `redeemed_at IS NULL AND revoked_at IS NULL`; a failed attempt is classified race-free into `AlreadyRevoked`/`Redeemed`/`NotFound` because those states are terminal). Backing `GET /v1/accounts/claim-codes` + `POST /v1/accounts/claim-codes/revoke` (admin companion's inventory screen).

lines: - `src/repo_backup.rs` — User-held repo backup (4 Tauri IPC commands — the "Back up your posts" section of the Media Backup screen, sibling of `blob_backup.rs`): `get_repo_backup_status(did)` (location + opt-in flag + snapshot size/rev), `set_repo_backup_enabled(did, enabled)`, `run_repo_backup(did)` (a full-CAR snapshot pass: `discover_pds` → `PdsClient::fetch_repo_car` over public `com.atproto.sync.getRepo` (`auth: none`, no session) → **validate the CAR client-side** (framing + every block hashing to its CID + exactly one root + a signed commit `version==3` bound to this DID + an intact MST walk — the client twin of `repo-engine`'s `car_import`, using the pure `cid`/`ipld-core`/`serde_ipld_dagcbor` primitives, NOT the repo-engine crate; the MST walk follows subtree + record-value links but never descends into records, since records link to out-of-CAR blobs) → atomic temp-file+rename write into `{root}/repo/{sanitized-did}.car` + a versioned manifest `{root}/repo/{sanitized-did}.json` (`rootCid, rev, sizeBytes, lastBackupAt`); idempotent — an unchanged `rev` skips the CAR rewrite and only advances the timestamp), and `export_repo_backup(did)` (read + **re-validate** the stored CAR; returns `{rootCid, rev, sizeBytes, lastBackupAt, carBase64}` for a caller to import — there is deliberately no "push to my live PDS" button, since `importRepo` needs a *deactivated* account, so restore flows through the migration machinery). A `pub(crate) mirror_repo_car(root, did) -> Option<Vec<u8>>` helper (the repo twin of `blob_backup::mirror_fallback_blob`, fail-closed re-validation) is the iCloud-mirror repo source consumed both by the normal outbound migration's `migration_orchestrator::transfer_repo` (source-`getRepo`-failure fallback) and by the sovereign disaster-recovery flow (`disaster_recovery::recovery_transfer_repo`). Reuses `blob_backup::resolve_backup_root`/`BackupLocation`/`sanitize_did` and the shared ubiquity container (no new entitlement). No encryption (the repo is public data on an `auth: none` endpoint) and, unlike the blob restore, no session — so `RepoBackupError` has **no `SESSION_LOCKED`**: (BACKUP_UNAVAILABLE, RATE_LIMITED, IDENTITY_NOT_FOUND, PLC_DIRECTORY_ERROR, SERVER_ERROR, NETWORK_ERROR, STORAGE_ERROR, MANIFEST_CORRUPT, CAR_INVALID, KEYCHAIN_ERROR)

- `src/self_held_kit.rs` — the **escrow-less self-held Shamir kit** (5 Tauri IPC commands — "Add a recovery key" on the identity screen): the `rekey.rs` ceremony minus the escrow, for a claimed identity whose device key holds `rotationKeys[0]` but whose host is not Custos. `build_self_held_kit(did)` (generate + stage a client-side seed / 2-of-3 v2 envelope split in the per-DID `self-held-kit-staging:{did}` slot BEFORE any network call, prove eligibility, return the additive diff + the host's URL), `submit_self_held_kit(did)` (device-key-sign a PLC rotation op inserting the derived recovery key directly after the device key — the whole current tail shifts down one index, nothing is removed — POST it to plc.directory, write Share 1 to the per-DID iCloud-synchronizable slot with read-back verify, refresh the cached log + doc, record the `{did}:self-held-kit` marker; biometric-gated in the frontend), `confirm_self_held_kit(did)` (teardown gate mirroring `confirm_rekey`: Share 1 must be verifiably durable before the staging slot — the last local home of Shares 2 and 3 — is destroyed), `self_held_kit_in_progress_cmd(did)`, and `self_held_kit_escrow_offer_cmd(did)` (the upsell **seam**: true only when the marker is present AND the identity's *current* host advertises `escrow`, so it is never true right after a kit completes). **Share 1 → Keychain; Shares 2 AND 3 → the user** — with no escrow there is no third party, and the sovereign recovery path already reconstructs from any two. **plc.directory is the only peer for anything touching the identity** (audit-log read, op submit, cache refresh); the sole request reaching the hosting PDS is the public, unauthenticated `describeServer` capability probe that proves the host offers no escrow — often served from the `pds_capabilities` cache, carrying no share material and no credential. No session, no `/v1/*` call, hence no `SESSION_LOCKED` and no `ESCROW_FAILED` in the error surface; user-facing copy must say "no share is sent to your server", never "your server is never contacted". `guard_self_held_kit_op` is the SEVENTH strict wallet allowlist and deliberately drops `guard_rekey_op`'s "current rotationKeys must be exactly 2" rule (which encodes the pre-inversion Custos `[device, PDS]` layout and would reject every claimed identity): device key pinned at `[0]`, the fresh recovery key inserted at `[1]`, the tail preserved verbatim, verificationMethods / services / alsoKnownAs byte-identical. `SelfHeldKitError` (NOT_DID_PLC, WALLET_NOT_AUTHORIZED, HOST_OFFERS_ESCROW, RATE_LIMITED, GUARD_REJECTED, INVALID_AUDIT_LOG, SHARE_GENERATION_FAILED, SIGNING_FAILED, PLC_SUBMISSION_FAILED, PLC_DIRECTORY_ERROR, SHARE_STORAGE_FAILED, SHARE_NOT_STORED, NETWORK_ERROR, IDENTITY_NOT_FOUND) serialized as `{ code: "SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE" }` with camelCase fields

- `src/recovery.rs` — Recovery override module: `build_recovery_override(pds_client, did, unauthorized_op_cid) -> Result<SignedRecoveryOp, RecoveryError>` (fetches audit log, identifies fork point, builds counter-operation restoring pre-unauthorized state, signs with per-DID device key), `submit_recovery_override(pds_client, did, signed_op) -> Result<ClaimResult, RecoveryError>` (POSTs to plc.directory, updates cached log and DID doc); Tauri IPC commands: `build_recovery_override_cmd`, `submit_recovery_override_cmd`. Types: `SignedRecoveryOp` { diff, signed_op }, `RecoveryState` { did, signed_op }, `RecoveryError` (RECOVERY_WINDOW_EXPIRED, SIGNING_FAILED, PLC_DIRECTORY_ERROR, NETWORK_ERROR, IDENTITY_NOT_FOUND, UNAUTHORIZED_CHANGE_NOT_FOUND)

-- `src/identity_removal.rs` — Permanent identity removal (5 Tauri IPC commands): `request_identity_removal(did)` (gets a full-access session via `SessionProvider::full_access_client` — a `NeedsUnlock` maps to `SessionRequired` so the UI runs `unlockIdentity` first — then calls `com.atproto.server.requestAccountDelete`, which emails a single-use code), `confirm_identity_removal(did, password, token)` (calls `deleteAccount` FIRST — a bad password/code is `InvalidToken` with nothing mutated — then persists a durable pending-removal marker and runs `retire_and_wipe`), `tombstone_identity(did)` (resume path: retire + wipe only, for when `confirm` deleted the account but the tombstone/wipe failed and the single-use code is already spent; for a did:web there is no tombstone to retry, so the resume is the local wipe alone), and `list_pending_removals()` (the launch-reconciliation source: the DIDs whose post-delete tombstone/wipe never finished), and `forget_identity_locally(did)` (the local-only escape hatch: wipes the DID's Keychain material and clears any pending marker with NO network step, returning `wasLastIdentity`. For an identity whose PDS account no longer exists — deleted from another device, purged server-side, or migrated away — `deleteAccount` can only answer with an opaque 401 indistinguishable from a wrong password (the PDS is not an account-existence oracle, see `crates/pds/src/routes/delete_account.rs`), so the request/confirm flow can never make progress. It deliberately does NOT tombstone the did:plc — the DID may already be retired or now live on another PDS — so it only promises to remove the identity from THIS device; biometric-gated in the frontend). Shared core `retire_and_wipe` is **method-aware** and owns the branch both commands go through: a **did:plc** runs `tombstone_and_wipe` (fetch the audit-log head as `prev`, build+sign a `crypto::build_did_plc_tombstone_op` with `per_did_sign_closure`, self-verified via `verify_plc_tombstone_op`, POST it to plc.directory, and ONLY THEN call `IdentityStore::remove_identity` — the wipe deletes the device key that signs the tombstone, so a submit failure must leave it intact for a retry; the `submit_then_wipe` ordering is unit-tested), while a **did:web** skips the tombstone leg entirely and goes straight to the wipe, never contacting plc.directory, reporting `tombstoneCid: None`. A did:web has no PLC log, so routing it through the tombstone path would 404 on the audit-log fetch and wedge the flow permanently: the account gone and its single-use email code spent, while the wipe — gated behind a submit that can never succeed — never runs and the pending-removal marker never clears, so every launch re-offers a doomed retry. The branch lives in the shared core rather than at the command boundary precisely because `tombstone_identity` (the resume path the marker routes to) reaches the same code; guarding only the entry point would leave the wedge reachable. Retiring a did:web network-wide means removing its `did.json` from the domain — an operator action outside the wallet's control, which the UI states rather than simulating. **Post-delete recovery marker:** the instant `deleteAccount` succeeds, `confirm_identity_removal` records the DID in the durable `pending-removals` Keychain index (a JSON array), *before* the tombstone's network round trip — the step iOS is most likely to interrupt by suspending the app. Both `confirm_identity_removal` and `tombstone_identity` clear the marker (best-effort) once `retire_and_wipe` completes — including on the did:web path, which is what keeps an interrupted did:web removal from becoming permanent retry state. On launch the UI calls `list_pending_removals()` and, for any listed DID, resumes straight to the idempotent retry rather than the request flow — which would fail against the already-deleted account. No PDS/DB changes: both `requestAccountDelete`/`deleteAccount` endpoints already exist and are method-agnostic, and the did:plc tombstone is the DID-level network messaging the PDS can't do (it holds no rotation key, ADR-0001). Types: `RemovalOutcome` { tombstoneCid (null when the removed DID has no tombstone leg — a did:web), wasLastIdentity }, `RemovalError` (SESSION_REQUIRED, REQUEST_DELETE_FAILED, INVALID_TOKEN, ACCOUNT_DELETE_FAILED, INVALID_AUDIT_LOG, TOMBSTONE_SIGNING_FAILED, PLC_DIRECTORY_ERROR, IDENTITY_NOT_FOUND, LOCAL_WIPE_FAILED, RATE_LIMITED, NETWORK_ERROR)

- `src/migrate.rs` — Self-signed account-migration identity leg (ADR-0002 path 1): builds and locally device-key-signs the DID-repointing PLC op and submits it directly to plc.directory — no email token, no `signPlcOperation` round-trip. `build_migration_op(pds_client, dest_client, did) -> Result<SignedMigrationOp, MigrateError>` (fetches audit log for `prev` + current state, reads `getRecommendedDidCredentials` from the DESTINATION PDS via the passed-in authed `OAuthClient`, assembles the op with the device key preserved at `rotationKeys[0]`, runs the strict pre-sign guard, signs with the per-DID device key), `submit_migration_op(pds_client, did, signed_op) -> Result<ClaimResult, MigrateError>` (POSTs to plc.directory, refreshes cached log + DID doc); Tauri IPC commands: `build_migration_op_cmd`, `submit_migration_op_cmd`. Pure helpers: `guard_migration_op` (strict allowlist), `recommended_verification_methods`/`recommended_services` (RecommendedCredentials JSON → typed maps), `latest_op_state` (current state from newest non-nullified audit entry), `build_migration_diff`. Types: `SignedMigrationOp` { diff, signed_op }, `MigrationState` { did, dest_oauth_client, signed_op }, `MigrationInputs`; `MigrateError` (WALLET_NOT_AUTHORIZED, GUARD_REJECTED, INVALID_RECOMMENDED_CREDENTIALS, INVALID_AUDIT_LOG, SIGNING_FAILED, PLC_DIRECTORY_ERROR, NETWORK_ERROR, IDENTITY_NOT_FOUND, MIGRATION_NOT_READY). The destination-PDS OAuth login is NOT owned here — the migration orchestrator authenticates and populates `MigrationState.dest_oauth_client` before `build_migration_op_cmd` runs

- `src/migration_orchestrator.rs` — wallet-authorized outbound migration state machine (ADR-0002 path 1). Fine-grained per-step Tauri commands driving the source→dest transfer: `prepare_migration` (resolve dest describeServer + source; returns `PreparedMigration { handle, sourcePdsUrl }` for the source-auth screen), `authenticate_migration_source` (password `createSession` → full-session Bearer client, mirrors `claim::authenticate_source_pds`; per ADR-0021 a full session is required to mint the source's `createAccount` service-auth token — HTTPS + account-match guards + email-2FA, password used once and never stored), `create_destination_account` (reserveSigningKey → getServiceAuth → deactivated `createAccount` → Bearer session; tolerates `DidAlreadyExists` for resume), `transfer_repo` (getRepo → importRepo; on a source `getRepo` failure it falls back to the local iCloud repo mirror `repo_backup::mirror_repo_car` when that mirror holds a CID/commit-valid snapshot for the DID, else surfaces the original source failure unchanged — the repo twin of the blob drain's mirror fallback), `transfer_blobs` (cursor-paginated `listMissingBlobs` drain), `transfer_preferences` (get→put), `verify_import` (`checkAccountStatus` completeness gate; returns `AccountStatus`), `arm_identity_leg` (populate `migrate::MigrationState.dest_oauth_client`, then run `migrate::build_migration_op_cmd`/`submit_migration_op_cmd`), `finalize_migration` (the safe cutover — **activate dest → durably persist the destination session → deactivate source → Finalized**; the source stays active until the durable credential is stored, so a crash or retry never strands the account credential-less). **Which credential gets persisted is capability-gated, not assumed**: `destination_credential` (pure, unit-tested) answers `Sovereign` or `Bearer` from the DID method plus the destination's advertised `sovereignSessions` (`pds_capabilities`, warm from `prepare_migration`'s describeServer). A host that **answered** and does not advertise it — the reference PDS, bsky.social, any spec-compliant PDS, or a Custos running with the capability off — takes the Bearer branch, since minting against a route it does not serve would fail *after* the identity op already landed. A did:web takes it unconditionally (no rotation keys to sign the proof). A host that could **not be asked** keeps the sovereign branch: `activateAccount` has already succeeded against it by then, so `reached: false` is a describeServer blink, not grounds to downgrade a Custos destination's credential. The same branch serves outbound migration and sovereign disaster recovery, which share this command. Pure cores split out for testability (`ensure_phase_did` gate, `create_destination_account_impl`, `drain_missing_blobs`, `transfer_repo_impl`, `transfer_preferences_impl`, `import_reconciles`, `activate_destination_account`/`deactivate_source_account` cutover halves, `destination_credential`, `ensure_sovereign_session_persisted` (idempotent skip when a persisted record's refresh token is still unexpired, else `sovereign_session::sovereign_login_impl` → persist), `ensure_bearer_session_persisted` (the same idempotent skip, then sub/aud-validate and persist the pair `createAccount` already issued into the same `{did}:oauth-tokens` record — from that write on `session_provider` restores and refreshes it identically, and re-unlock rides `password_unlock`'s password `createSession` route), and the `*_core` mutex-parameterized command cores; `finalize_migration_core` takes an injected `ensure_session` step so its activate → session → deactivate ordering is unit-testable without a Keychain or live PDS, and `finalize_migration_impl` sits above it holding the whole snapshot → capability probe → branch → cutover path, so everything the Tauri command does bar unwrapping `State` is drivable against mock servers — which is what proves the non-Custos cutover never calls `/v1/sessions/sovereign`). `MigrationError` (MIGRATION_NOT_READY, DESTINATION_UNREACHABLE, SOURCE_AUTH_FAILED, TWO_FACTOR_REQUIRED, ACCOUNT_MISMATCH, INSECURE_SOURCE_URL, RATE_LIMITED, SERVER_ERROR, SERVICE_AUTH_FAILED, ACCOUNT_CREATION_FAILED, DESTINATION_CONFLICT, REPO_TRANSFER_FAILED, BLOB_TRANSFER_FAILED, PREFERENCES_TRANSFER_FAILED, VERIFICATION_INCOMPLETE, ACTIVATION_FAILED, SOVEREIGN_LOGIN_FAILED, SESSION_PERSIST_FAILED, DEACTIVATION_FAILED, NETWORK_ERROR — SOVEREIGN_LOGIN_FAILED and SESSION_PERSIST_FAILED are the retryable cutover-mint failures that leave the source active, aborting before deactivation). Migration state is in-memory only (`AppState.orchestration_state`); an app kill restarts from `prepare_migration`, but the destination session it persists (via `identity_store` `{did}:oauth-tokens`) survives — a restarted wallet reconstructs the destination client from that record (`sovereign_session::stored_bearer_client`), not from `OutboundMigrationState`. The orchestrator never POSTs plc.directory — the single PLC write is `migrate::submit_migration_op_cmd`

lines: - `src/repo_backup.rs` — User-held repo backup (4 Tauri IPC commands — the "Back up your posts" section of the Media Backup screen, sibling of `blob_backup.rs`): `get_repo_backup_status(did)` (location + opt-in flag + snapshot size/rev), `set_repo_backup_enabled(did, enabled)`, `run_repo_backup(did)` (a full-CAR snapshot pass: `discover_pds` → `PdsClient::fetch_repo_car` over public `com.atproto.sync.getRepo` (`auth: none`, no session) → **validate the CAR client-side** (framing + every block hashing to its CID + exactly one root + a signed commit `version==3` bound to this DID + an intact MST walk — the client twin of `repo-engine`'s `car_import`, using the pure `cid`/`ipld-core`/`serde_ipld_dagcbor` primitives, NOT the repo-engine crate; the MST walk follows subtree + record-value links but never descends into records, since records link to out-of-CAR blobs) → atomic temp-file+rename write into `{root}/repo/{sanitized-did}.car` + a versioned manifest `{root}/repo/{sanitized-did}.json` (`rootCid, rev, sizeBytes, lastBackupAt`); idempotent — an unchanged `rev` skips the CAR rewrite and only advances the timestamp), and `export_repo_backup(did)` (read + **re-validate** the stored CAR; returns `{rootCid, rev, sizeBytes, lastBackupAt, carBase64}` for a caller to import — there is deliberately no "push to my live PDS" button, since `importRepo` needs a *deactivated* account, so restore flows through the migration machinery). A `pub(crate) mirror_repo_car(root, did) -> Option<Vec<u8>>` helper (the repo twin of `blob_backup::mirror_fallback_blob`, fail-closed re-validation) is the iCloud-mirror repo source consumed both by the normal outbound migration's `migration_orchestrator::transfer_repo` (source-`getRepo`-failure fallback) and by the sovereign disaster-recovery flow (`disaster_recovery::recovery_transfer_repo`). Reuses `blob_backup::resolve_backup_root`/`BackupLocation`/`sanitize_did` and the shared ubiquity container (no new entitlement). No encryption (the repo is public data on an `auth: none` endpoint) and, unlike the blob restore, no session — so `RepoBackupError` has **no `SESSION_LOCKED`**: (BACKUP_UNAVAILABLE, RATE_LIMITED, IDENTITY_NOT_FOUND, PLC_DIRECTORY_ERROR, SERVER_ERROR, NETWORK_ERROR, STORAGE_ERROR, MANIFEST_CORRUPT, CAR_INVALID, KEYCHAIN_ERROR)

- `src/self_held_kit.rs` — the **escrow-less self-held Shamir kit** (5 Tauri IPC commands — "Add a recovery key" on the identity screen): the `rekey.rs` ceremony minus the escrow, for a claimed identity whose device key holds `rotationKeys[0]` but whose host is not Custos. `build_self_held_kit(did)` (generate + stage a client-side seed / 2-of-3 v2 envelope split in the per-DID `self-held-kit-staging:{did}` slot BEFORE any network call, prove eligibility, return the additive diff + the host's URL), `submit_self_held_kit(did)` (device-key-sign a PLC rotation op inserting the derived recovery key directly after the device key — the whole current tail shifts down one index, nothing is removed — POST it to plc.directory, write Share 1 to the per-DID iCloud-synchronizable slot with read-back verify, refresh the cached log + doc, record the `{did}:self-held-kit` marker; biometric-gated in the frontend), `confirm_self_held_kit(did)` (teardown gate mirroring `confirm_rekey`: Share 1 must be verifiably durable before the staging slot — the last local home of Shares 2 and 3 — is destroyed), `self_held_kit_in_progress_cmd(did)`, and `self_held_kit_escrow_offer_cmd(did)` (the upsell **seam**: true only when the marker is present AND the identity's *current* host advertises `escrow`, so it is never true right after a kit completes). **Share 1 → Keychain; Shares 2 AND 3 → the user** — with no escrow there is no third party, and the sovereign recovery path already reconstructs from any two. **plc.directory is the only peer for anything touching the identity** (audit-log read, op submit, cache refresh); the sole request reaching the hosting PDS is the public, unauthenticated `describeServer` capability probe that proves the host offers no escrow — often served from the `pds_capabilities` cache, carrying no share material and no credential. No session, no `/v1/*` call, hence no `SESSION_LOCKED` and no `ESCROW_FAILED` in the error surface; user-facing copy must say "no share is sent to your server", never "your server is never contacted". `guard_self_held_kit_op` is the SEVENTH strict wallet allowlist and deliberately drops `guard_rekey_op`'s "current rotationKeys must be exactly 2" rule (which encodes the pre-inversion Custos `[device, PDS]` layout and would reject every claimed identity): device key pinned at `[0]`, the fresh recovery key inserted at `[1]`, the tail preserved verbatim, verificationMethods / services / alsoKnownAs byte-identical. `SelfHeldKitError` (NOT_DID_PLC, WALLET_NOT_AUTHORIZED, HOST_OFFERS_ESCROW, RATE_LIMITED, GUARD_REJECTED, INVALID_AUDIT_LOG, SHARE_GENERATION_FAILED, SIGNING_FAILED, PLC_SUBMISSION_FAILED, PLC_DIRECTORY_ERROR, SHARE_STORAGE_FAILED, SHARE_NOT_STORED, NETWORK_ERROR, IDENTITY_NOT_FOUND) serialized as `{ code: "SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE" }` with camelCase fields

- `src/recovery.rs` — Recovery override module: `build_recovery_override(pds_client, did, unauthorized_op_cid) -> Result<SignedRecoveryOp, RecoveryError>` (fetches audit log, identifies fork point, builds counter-operation restoring pre-unauthorized state, signs with per-DID device key), `submit_recovery_override(pds_client, did, signed_op) -> Result<ClaimResult, RecoveryError>` (POSTs to plc.directory, updates cached log and DID doc); Tauri IPC commands: `build_recovery_override_cmd`, `submit_recovery_override_cmd`. Types: `SignedRecoveryOp` { diff, signed_op }, `RecoveryState` { did, signed_op }, `RecoveryError` (RECOVERY_WINDOW_EXPIRED, SIGNING_FAILED, PLC_DIRECTORY_ERROR, NETWORK_ERROR, IDENTITY_NOT_FOUND, UNAUTHORIZED_CHANGE_NOT_FOUND)

-- `src/identity_removal.rs` — Permanent identity removal (6 Tauri IPC commands): `get_identity_removal_route(did) -> RemovalRoute { requiresPassword, pdsUrl }` (which credential this identity's removal needs — `requiresPassword: false` when the host advertises `walletAccountDelete` and the wallet can sign the removal itself; resolved through the **same** `resolve_pds_url` the confirm step uses, so the screen and the request can never address different hosts; a host that could not be described reports `true`, since a field the user can ignore beats a missing one), `request_identity_removal(did)` (gets a full-access session via `SessionProvider::full_access_client` — a `NeedsUnlock` maps to `SessionRequired` so the UI runs `unlockIdentity` first — then calls `com.atproto.server.requestAccountDelete`, which emails a single-use code), `confirm_identity_removal(did, password, token)` (calls `deleteAccount` FIRST — a bad password/code is `InvalidToken` with nothing mutated — then persists a durable pending-removal marker and runs `retire_and_wipe`), `tombstone_identity(did)` (resume path: retire + wipe only, for when `confirm` deleted the account but the tombstone/wipe failed and the single-use code is already spent; for a did:web there is no tombstone to retry, so the resume is the local wipe alone), and `list_pending_removals()` (the launch-reconciliation source: the DIDs whose post-delete tombstone/wipe never finished), and `forget_identity_locally(did)` (the local-only escape hatch: wipes the DID's Keychain material and clears any pending marker with NO network step, returning `wasLastIdentity`. For an identity whose PDS account no longer exists — deleted from another device, purged server-side, or migrated away — `deleteAccount` can only answer with an opaque 401 indistinguishable from a wrong password (the PDS is not an account-existence oracle, see `crates/pds/src/routes/delete_account.rs`), so the request/confirm flow can never make progress. It deliberately does NOT tombstone the did:plc — the DID may already be retired or now live on another PDS — so it only promises to remove the identity from THIS device; biometric-gated in the frontend). Shared core `retire_and_wipe` is **method-aware** and owns the branch both commands go through: a **did:plc** runs `tombstone_and_wipe` (fetch the audit-log head as `prev`, build+sign a `crypto::build_did_plc_tombstone_op` with `per_did_sign_closure`, self-verified via `verify_plc_tombstone_op`, POST it to plc.directory, and ONLY THEN call `IdentityStore::remove_identity` — the wipe deletes the device key that signs the tombstone, so a submit failure must leave it intact for a retry; the `submit_then_wipe` ordering is unit-tested), while a **did:web** skips the tombstone leg entirely and goes straight to the wipe, never contacting plc.directory, reporting `tombstoneCid: None`. A did:web has no PLC log, so routing it through the tombstone path would 404 on the audit-log fetch and wedge the flow permanently: the account gone and its single-use email code spent, while the wipe — gated behind a submit that can never succeed — never runs and the pending-removal marker never clears, so every launch re-offers a doomed retry. The branch lives in the shared core rather than at the command boundary precisely because `tombstone_identity` (the resume path the marker routes to) reaches the same code; guarding only the entry point would leave the wedge reachable. Retiring a did:web network-wide means removing its `did.json` from the domain — an operator action outside the wallet's control, which the UI states rather than simulating. **Post-delete recovery marker:** the instant `deleteAccount` succeeds, `confirm_identity_removal` records the DID in the durable `pending-removals` Keychain index (a JSON array), *before* the tombstone's network round trip — the step iOS is most likely to interrupt by suspending the app. Both `confirm_identity_removal` and `tombstone_identity` clear the marker (best-effort) once `retire_and_wipe` completes — including on the did:web path, which is what keeps an interrupted did:web removal from becoming permanent retry state. On launch the UI calls `list_pending_removals()` and, for any listed DID, resumes straight to the idempotent retry rather than the request flow — which would fail against the already-deleted account. No PDS/DB changes: both `requestAccountDelete`/`deleteAccount` endpoints already exist and are method-agnostic, and the did:plc tombstone is the DID-level network messaging the PDS can't do (it holds no rotation key, ADR-0001). Types: `RemovalOutcome` { tombstoneCid (null when the removed DID has no tombstone leg — a did:web), wasLastIdentity }, `RemovalError` (SESSION_REQUIRED, REQUEST_DELETE_FAILED, INVALID_TOKEN, ACCOUNT_DELETE_FAILED, INVALID_AUDIT_LOG, TOMBSTONE_SIGNING_FAILED, PLC_DIRECTORY_ERROR, IDENTITY_NOT_FOUND, LOCAL_WIPE_FAILED, RATE_LIMITED, NETWORK_ERROR)

- `src/migrate.rs` — Self-signed account-migration identity leg (ADR-0002 path 1): builds and locally device-key-signs the DID-repointing PLC op and submits it directly to plc.directory — no email token, no `signPlcOperation` round-trip. `build_migration_op(pds_client, dest_client, did) -> Result<SignedMigrationOp, MigrateError>` (fetches audit log for `prev` + current state, reads `getRecommendedDidCredentials` from the DESTINATION PDS via the passed-in authed `OAuthClient`, assembles the op with the device key preserved at `rotationKeys[0]`, runs the strict pre-sign guard, signs with the per-DID device key), `submit_migration_op(pds_client, did, signed_op) -> Result<ClaimResult, MigrateError>` (POSTs to plc.directory, refreshes cached log + DID doc); Tauri IPC commands: `build_migration_op_cmd`, `submit_migration_op_cmd`. Pure helpers: `guard_migration_op` (strict allowlist), `recommended_verification_methods`/`recommended_services` (RecommendedCredentials JSON → typed maps), `latest_op_state` (current state from newest non-nullified audit entry), `build_migration_diff`. Types: `SignedMigrationOp` { diff, signed_op }, `MigrationState` { did, dest_oauth_client, signed_op }, `MigrationInputs`; `MigrateError` (WALLET_NOT_AUTHORIZED, GUARD_REJECTED, INVALID_RECOMMENDED_CREDENTIALS, INVALID_AUDIT_LOG, SIGNING_FAILED, PLC_DIRECTORY_ERROR, NETWORK_ERROR, IDENTITY_NOT_FOUND, MIGRATION_NOT_READY). The destination-PDS OAuth login is NOT owned here — the migration orchestrator authenticates and populates `MigrationState.dest_oauth_client` before `build_migration_op_cmd` runs

- `src/migration_orchestrator.rs` — wallet-authorized outbound migration state machine (ADR-0002 path 1). Fine-grained per-step Tauri commands driving the source→dest transfer: `prepare_migration` (resolve dest describeServer + source; returns `PreparedMigration { handle, sourcePdsUrl }` for the source-auth screen), `authenticate_migration_source` (password `createSession` → full-session Bearer client, mirrors `claim::authenticate_source_pds`; per ADR-0021 a full session is required to mint the source's `createAccount` service-auth token — HTTPS + account-match guards + email-2FA, password used once and never stored), `create_destination_account` (reserveSigningKey → getServiceAuth → deactivated `createAccount` → Bearer session; tolerates `DidAlreadyExists` for resume), `transfer_repo` (getRepo → importRepo; on a source `getRepo` failure it falls back to the local iCloud repo mirror `repo_backup::mirror_repo_car` when that mirror holds a CID/commit-valid snapshot for the DID, else surfaces the original source failure unchanged — the repo twin of the blob drain's mirror fallback), `transfer_blobs` (cursor-paginated `listMissingBlobs` drain), `transfer_preferences` (get→put), `verify_import` (`checkAccountStatus` completeness gate; returns `AccountStatus`), `arm_identity_leg` (populate `migrate::MigrationState.dest_oauth_client`, then run `migrate::build_migration_op_cmd`/`submit_migration_op_cmd`), `finalize_migration` (the safe cutover — **activate dest → durably persist the destination session → deactivate source → Finalized**; the source stays active until the durable credential is stored, so a crash or retry never strands the account credential-less). **Which credential gets persisted is capability-gated, not assumed**: `destination_credential` (pure, unit-tested) answers `Sovereign` or `Bearer` from the DID method plus the destination's advertised `sovereignSessions` (`pds_capabilities`, warm from `prepare_migration`'s describeServer). A host that **answered** and does not advertise it — the reference PDS, bsky.social, any spec-compliant PDS, or a Custos running with the capability off — takes the Bearer branch, since minting against a route it does not serve would fail *after* the identity op already landed. A did:web takes it unconditionally (no rotation keys to sign the proof). A host that could **not be asked** keeps the sovereign branch: `activateAccount` has already succeeded against it by then, so `reached: false` is a describeServer blink, not grounds to downgrade a Custos destination's credential. The same branch serves outbound migration and sovereign disaster recovery, which share this command. lines: - `src/repo_backup.rs` — User-held repo backup (4 Tauri IPC commands — the "Back up your posts" section of the Media Backup screen, sibling of `blob_backup.rs`): `get_repo_backup_status(did)` (location + opt-in flag + snapshot size/rev), `set_repo_backup_enabled(did, enabled)`, `run_repo_backup(did)` (a full-CAR snapshot pass: `discover_pds` → `PdsClient::fetch_repo_car` over public `com.atproto.sync.getRepo` (`auth: none`, no session) → **validate the CAR client-side** (framing + every block hashing to its CID + exactly one root + a signed commit `version==3` bound to this DID + an intact MST walk — the client twin of `repo-engine`'s `car_import`, using the pure `cid`/`ipld-core`/`serde_ipld_dagcbor` primitives, NOT the repo-engine crate; the MST walk follows subtree + record-value links but never descends into records, since records link to out-of-CAR blobs) → atomic temp-file+rename write into `{root}/repo/{sanitized-did}.car` + a versioned manifest `{root}/repo/{sanitized-did}.json` (`rootCid, rev, sizeBytes, lastBackupAt`); idempotent — an unchanged `rev` skips the CAR rewrite and only advances the timestamp), and `export_repo_backup(did)` (read + **re-validate** the stored CAR; returns `{rootCid, rev, sizeBytes, lastBackupAt, carBase64}` for a caller to import — there is deliberately no "push to my live PDS" button, since `importRepo` needs a *deactivated* account, so restore flows through the migration machinery). A `pub(crate) mirror_repo_car(root, did) -> Option<Vec<u8>>` helper (the repo twin of `blob_backup::mirror_fallback_blob`, fail-closed re-validation) is the iCloud-mirror repo source consumed both by the normal outbound migration's `migration_orchestrator::transfer_repo` (source-`getRepo`-failure fallback) and by the sovereign disaster-recovery flow (`disaster_recovery::recovery_transfer_repo`). Reuses `blob_backup::resolve_backup_root`/`BackupLocation`/`sanitize_did` and the shared ubiquity container (no new entitlement). No encryption (the repo is public data on an `auth: none` endpoint) and, unlike the blob restore, no session — so `RepoBackupError` has **no `SESSION_LOCKED`**: (BACKUP_UNAVAILABLE, RATE_LIMITED, IDENTITY_NOT_FOUND, PLC_DIRECTORY_ERROR, SERVER_ERROR, NETWORK_ERROR, STORAGE_ERROR, MANIFEST_CORRUPT, CAR_INVALID, KEYCHAIN_ERROR)

- `src/self_held_kit.rs` — the **escrow-less self-held Shamir kit** (5 Tauri IPC commands — "Add a recovery key" on the identity screen): the `rekey.rs` ceremony minus the escrow, for a claimed identity whose device key holds `rotationKeys[0]` but whose host is not Custos. `build_self_held_kit(did)` (generate + stage a client-side seed / 2-of-3 v2 envelope split in the per-DID `self-held-kit-staging:{did}` slot BEFORE any network call, prove eligibility, return the additive diff + the host's URL), `submit_self_held_kit(did)` (device-key-sign a PLC rotation op inserting the derived recovery key directly after the device key — the whole current tail shifts down one index, nothing is removed — POST it to plc.directory, write Share 1 to the per-DID iCloud-synchronizable slot with read-back verify, refresh the cached log + doc, record the `{did}:self-held-kit` marker; biometric-gated in the frontend), `confirm_self_held_kit(did)` (teardown gate mirroring `confirm_rekey`: Share 1 must be verifiably durable before the staging slot — the last local home of Shares 2 and 3 — is destroyed), `self_held_kit_in_progress_cmd(did)`, and `self_held_kit_escrow_offer_cmd(did)` (the upsell **seam**: true only when the marker is present AND the identity's *current* host advertises `escrow`, so it is never true right after a kit completes). **Share 1 → Keychain; Shares 2 AND 3 → the user** — with no escrow there is no third party, and the sovereign recovery path already reconstructs from any two. **plc.directory is the only peer for anything touching the identity** (audit-log read, op submit, cache refresh); the sole request reaching the hosting PDS is the public, unauthenticated `describeServer` capability probe that proves the host offers no escrow — often served from the `pds_capabilities` cache, carrying no share material and no credential. No session, no `/v1/*` call, hence no `SESSION_LOCKED` and no `ESCROW_FAILED` in the error surface; user-facing copy must say "no share is sent to your server", never "your server is never contacted". `guard_self_held_kit_op` is the SEVENTH strict wallet allowlist and deliberately drops `guard_rekey_op`'s "current rotationKeys must be exactly 2" rule (which encodes the pre-inversion Custos `[device, PDS]` layout and would reject every claimed identity): device key pinned at `[0]`, the fresh recovery key inserted at `[1]`, the tail preserved verbatim, verificationMethods / services / alsoKnownAs byte-identical. `SelfHeldKitError` (NOT_DID_PLC, WALLET_NOT_AUTHORIZED, HOST_OFFERS_ESCROW, RATE_LIMITED, GUARD_REJECTED, INVALID_AUDIT_LOG, SHARE_GENERATION_FAILED, SIGNING_FAILED, PLC_SUBMISSION_FAILED, PLC_DIRECTORY_ERROR, SHARE_STORAGE_FAILED, SHARE_NOT_STORED, NETWORK_ERROR, IDENTITY_NOT_FOUND) serialized as `{ code: "SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE" }` with camelCase fields

- `src/recovery.rs` — Recovery override module: `build_recovery_override(pds_client, did, unauthorized_op_cid) -> Result<SignedRecoveryOp, RecoveryError>` (fetches audit log, identifies fork point, builds counter-operation restoring pre-unauthorized state, signs with per-DID device key), `submit_recovery_override(pds_client, did, signed_op) -> Result<ClaimResult, RecoveryError>` (POSTs to plc.directory, updates cached log and DID doc); Tauri IPC commands: `build_recovery_override_cmd`, `submit_recovery_override_cmd`. Types: `SignedRecoveryOp` { diff, signed_op }, `RecoveryState` { did, signed_op }, `RecoveryError` (RECOVERY_WINDOW_EXPIRED, SIGNING_FAILED, PLC_DIRECTORY_ERROR, NETWORK_ERROR, IDENTITY_NOT_FOUND, UNAUTHORIZED_CHANGE_NOT_FOUND)

-- `src/identity_removal.rs` — Permanent identity removal (6 Tauri IPC commands): `get_identity_removal_route(did) -> RemovalRoute { requiresPassword, pdsUrl }` (which credential this identity's removal needs — `requiresPassword: false` when the host advertises `walletAccountDelete` and the wallet can sign the removal itself; resolved through the **same** `resolve_pds_url` the confirm step uses, so the screen and the request can never address different hosts; a host that could not be described reports `true`, since a field the user can ignore beats a missing one), `request_identity_removal(did)` (gets a full-access session via `SessionProvider::full_access_client` — a `NeedsUnlock` maps to `SessionRequired` so the UI runs `unlockIdentity` first — then calls `com.atproto.server.requestAccountDelete`, which emails a single-use code), `confirm_identity_removal(did, password: Option<String>, token)` (calls `deleteAccount` FIRST — a bad credential mutates nothing — then persists a durable pending-removal marker and runs `retire_and_wipe`. `password: None` is an identity that has none: `build_delete_credential` then device-key-signs `crypto::encode_account_delete_envelope` — audience = the host's own `describeServer` DID, so a proof cannot be relayed to another server — and sends it as the body's off-lexicon `custos.proof`, gated on the host advertising `walletAccountDelete` (`PasswordRequired` otherwise, before anything is signed or sent). One `describeServer` answers both halves the proof needs — whether the host reads it, and the audience DID — so an unreachable host surfaces as the network failure it is rather than as a demand for a password the identity may not have. The server's refusal is deliberately identical for a bad password and a bad proof, so the wallet distinguishes them from what it *sent*: `InvalidToken` when a password went, `InvalidConfirmationCode` when a proof did — an identity with no password is never told to check one), `tombstone_identity(did)` (resume path: retire + wipe only, for when `confirm` deleted the account but the tombstone/wipe failed and the single-use code is already spent; for a did:web there is no tombstone to retry, so the resume is the local wipe alone), and `list_pending_removals()` (the launch-reconciliation source: the DIDs whose post-delete tombstone/wipe never finished), and `forget_identity_locally(did)` (the local-only escape hatch: wipes the DID's Keychain material and clears any pending marker with NO network step, returning `wasLastIdentity`. For an identity whose PDS account no longer exists — deleted from another device, purged server-side, or migrated away — `deleteAccount` can only answer with an opaque 401 indistinguishable from a wrong password (the PDS is not an account-existence oracle, see `crates/pds/src/routes/delete_account.rs`), so the request/confirm flow can never make progress. It deliberately does NOT tombstone the did:plc — the DID may already be retired or now live on another PDS — so it only promises to remove the identity from THIS device; biometric-gated in the frontend). Shared core `retire_and_wipe` is **method-aware** and owns the branch both commands go through: a **did:plc** runs `tombstone_and_wipe` (fetch the audit-log head as `prev`, build+sign a `crypto::build_did_plc_tombstone_op` with `per_did_sign_closure`, self-verified via `verify_plc_tombstone_op`, POST it to plc.directory, and ONLY THEN call `IdentityStore::remove_identity` — the wipe deletes the device key that signs the tombstone, so a submit failure must leave it intact for a retry; the `submit_then_wipe` ordering is unit-tested), while a **did:web** skips the tombstone leg entirely and goes straight to the wipe, never contacting plc.directory, reporting `tombstoneCid: None`. A did:web has no PLC log, so routing it through the tombstone path would 404 on the audit-log fetch and wedge the flow permanently: the account gone and its single-use email code spent, while the wipe — gated behind a submit that can never succeed — never runs and the pending-removal marker never clears, so every launch re-offers a doomed retry. The branch lives in the shared core rather than at the command boundary precisely because `tombstone_identity` (the resume path the marker routes to) reaches the same code; guarding only the entry point would leave the wedge reachable. Retiring a did:web network-wide means removing its `did.json` from the domain — an operator action outside the wallet's control, which the UI states rather than simulating. **Post-delete recovery marker:** the instant `deleteAccount` succeeds, `confirm_identity_removal` records the DID in the durable `pending-removals` Keychain index (a JSON array), *before* the tombstone's network round trip — the step iOS is most likely to interrupt by suspending the app. Both `confirm_identity_removal` and `tombstone_identity` clear the marker (best-effort) once `retire_and_wipe` completes — including on the did:web path, which is what keeps an interrupted did:web removal from becoming permanent retry state. On launch the UI calls `list_pending_removals()` and, for any listed DID, resumes straight to the idempotent retry rather than the request flow — which would fail against the already-deleted account. No PDS/DB changes: both `requestAccountDelete`/`deleteAccount` endpoints already exist and are method-agnostic, and the did:plc tombstone is the DID-level network messaging the PDS can't do (it holds no rotation key, ADR-0001). - `src/migrate.rs` — Self-signed account-migration identity leg (ADR-0002 path 1): builds and locally device-key-signs the DID-repointing PLC op and submits it directly to plc.directory — no email token, no `signPlcOperation` round-trip. `build_migration_op(pds_client, dest_client, did) -> Result<SignedMigrationOp, MigrateError>` (fetches audit log for `prev` + current state, reads `getRecommendedDidCredentials` from the DESTINATION PDS via the passed-in authed `OAuthClient`, assembles the op with the device key preserved at `rotationKeys[0]`, runs the strict pre-sign guard, signs with the per-DID device key), `submit_migration_op(pds_client, did, signed_op) -> Result<ClaimResult, MigrateError>` (POSTs to plc.directory, refreshes cached log + DID doc); Tauri IPC commands: `build_migration_op_cmd`, `submit_migration_op_cmd`. 1	// pattern: Imperative Shell
2	//
3	// Gathers: DB pool + firehose via AppState, JSON body { did, password, token, custos? }
4	// Processes: validate body → verify the credential factor (account password, or a device-key-signed
5	//            deletion proof) → consume the single-use email token → permanently delete the account
6	//            (all local data) and emit an `#account` (deleted) frame
7	// Returns: 200 OK (empty) on success; ApiError on failure
8	//
9	// Implements: POST /xrpc/com.atproto.server.deleteAccount
10	//
11	// Unlike deactivate/activate, this endpoint is **not** session-authenticated: the credentials are
12	// in the body (a user must be able to delete an account they can no longer log a session into).
13	// The email `token` (minted by `requestAccountDelete`) is always one of the two factors. The other
14	// is whichever the *request* presents:
15	//
16	//   * the account `password` — the standard lexicon field, unchanged; or
17	//   * a **deletion proof** — a fresh timestamped envelope (`crypto::encode_account_delete_envelope`)
18	//     signed by a key in the account's authoritative current signing authority
19	//     (`identity::authority`: a did:plc rotation set, or a self-hosted did:web's `#device` key),
20	//     carried in the off-lexicon `custos` extension object.
21	//
22	// The proof exists because an account created with no password (the `optionalPassword` capability)
23	// could otherwise never be deleted at all: every credential path folded into the same 401 and the
24	// holder had no way forward. It is accepted for a passworded account too — selecting the factor by
25	// what the request presents rather than by what the account has. A current rotation key is already
26	// the highest authority over the identity (it can migrate or tombstone the DID outright), so
27	// refusing it to an account that also happens to have a password would deny the stronger credential
28	// while honouring the weaker one, and would make the endpoint answer differently depending on
29	// whether a password exists — the oracle this route exists to avoid.
30	//
31	// The heavy lifting — the multi-table atomic delete, the firehose frame, and on-disk blob
32	// reclamation — lives in `account_delete::purge_account`, shared with the scheduled-deletion reaper.
33

content.text:
Done. All gates green.

## What shipped

**The gap:** a `NULL password_hash` account had no credential path to `deleteAccount` — every branch folded into the same 401. That was latent until MM-481 landed `optionalPassword`; it would have minted accounts nobody could remove.

**Server** — [delete_account.rs](crates/pds/src/routes/delete_account.rs) now selects its first factor from what the *request* presents: the standard `password`, or a **deletion proof** in an off-lexicon `custos.proof` object. The proof is a new domain-versioned envelope ([account_delete.rs](crates/crypto/src/account_delete.rs), golden vector shared with the wallet) verified through the existing `identity::authority` — the same live-plc.directory lookup sovereign sessions and OAuth consent use, never a cached doc. The email token is unchanged and still second.

**Wallet** — `confirm_identity_removal` takes an optional password and signs the envelope when the host advertises the capability; a new `get_identity_removal_route` tells the screen which credential to collect, resolved through the *same* `resolve_pds_url` the deletion will address so the screen and the request can't disagree.

## Two deliberate deviations from the issue text

1. **The proof is accepted for passworded accounts too**, not gated on `password_hash IS NULL`. A current rotation key can already migrate or tombstone the DID outright, so it is the stronger credential — and branching on whether a password exists would make the endpoint answer differently per account, which is the oracle this route exists to avoid.

2. **A new `walletAccountDelete` capability** rather than reusing `optionalPassword` as the issue suggested. The wallet's real question is "will this host accept a signature here?", and `optionalPassword` only answers "may new accounts skip a password" — it can't tell the wallet whether *this* account has one. Say the word if you'd rather I collapse them.

## Verification

- 2769 PDS-lane tests, 690 wallet Rust tests, 229 frontend tests, clippy `-D warnings`, fmt, iOS cross-compile, and `docs-check`/`bruno-check`/`capability-docs-check`/`ticket-ref-check`/`lock-check` — all pass.
- Six new route tests cover each AC: passwordless deletion succeeds and emits the tombstone frame; a replayed proof is refused *even when paired with a valid token* (the nonce is spent before the token and not rolled back, so a captured envelope can't be re-aimed at a token obtained later); a proof bound to DID A can't delete DID B; unknown-DID / wrong-password / bad-proof responses are asserted **byte-identical**; no credential failure consumes the token. The six original tests pass unmodified.
- Driven live in the browser harness: on a `walletAccountDelete` host the confirm step renders one field (screenshot above), and on `self-held-kit` (host advertises nothing) both fields return. No console errors.

**Not verified end-to-end:** I drove the UI to the confirm step but didn't complete a fake removal through tombstone + wipe — that tail is untouched by this change and covered by the existing wallet tests.

Nothing committed or pushed. Want me to open a PR (which will also move MM-479 to In Review)?

input.command:
git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
Passwordless accounts: delete with a device-key proof (MM-479)

An account with a NULL password_hash could not be deleted. deleteAccount
verified the password before consuming the email token, and the no-password
case folded into the same uniform 401 as every other credential failure — so
the holder saw a refusal with nothing behind it and no path forward. Latent
until optionalPassword shipped; reachable the moment it did.

deleteAccount now picks its first factor from what the request presents. The
password branch is unchanged. A request may instead carry a deletion proof —
a fresh timestamped envelope (crypto::encode_account_delete_envelope, a new
domain-versioned encoder in the sovereign-session/oauth-consent mold, with a
golden vector shared with the wallet) verified through identity::authority,
the same authoritative live-plc.directory rotation-set lookup the other two
passwordless surfaces use. The cached DID document is never consulted. The
emailed token remains the second factor either way, and is still redeemed
only after the first one holds.

The proof is accepted for passworded accounts too. Selecting on what the
request presents rather than on what the account has is deliberate: a current
rotation key can already migrate or tombstone the DID outright, so refusing
it to an account that also has a password would honour the weaker credential
over the stronger — and would make the endpoint answer differently depending
on whether a password exists, which is the oracle this route exists to avoid.
Unknown DID, wrong password, and bad proof stay byte-identical responses.

The proof's nonce is spent in sovereign_session_nonces before the token is
redeemed, and is not rolled back by a token failure. That ordering is what
makes an envelope single-use in its own right rather than single-use only if
the other factor happened to hold: a captured proof replayed later against a
token the attacker has since obtained lands on a nonce already seen. The
store is shared with sovereign sessions — the domain-versioned envelopes make
nonces non-transferable across surfaces anyway, and reusing it keeps these
rows on the account-purge path already covered by the schema-walking test.

Advertised as the walletAccountDelete capability (always on, the same
key-sovereign trust model as sovereignSessions). It is advertised separately
rather than folded into optionalPassword because a client's real question is
"will this host accept a signature here?", which optionalPassword cannot
answer — it describes account creation, and cannot tell a wallet whether a
given account has a password.

Wallet: confirm_identity_removal takes an optional password and signs the
envelope when the host advertises the capability; get_identity_removal_route
tells the removal screen which credential to collect, resolved through the
same resolve_pds_url the deletion itself will address so the screen and the
request can never reach different hosts. The screen drops the password field
where it does not apply, and a credential refusal reads as
INVALID_CONFIRMATION_CODE rather than INVALID_TOKEN when a proof was sent —
the server cannot tell the two apart, but the wallet knows what it sent, and
an identity with no password must never be told to check one.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
